title: dsh-ee extension manifest dsh-ee.extension.json
description: Placed in the extension root directory. After writing it, check it with `dsh-ee extension check <dir> --json`; it is valid only when every check passes. Design: docs/plugins.md §5.

text.description: Human-readable text. Either a single string or one string per language. For internal enterprise use, a single string is enough; provide both Chinese and English when distributing publicly.

id.description: Extension identity: author/name. Use a short company or organization name as the author (for internal use, the company short name); lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only.

version.description: Semantic version. After delivering the extension to an administrator, bump the version whenever the manifest or the API document changes; there is no need to bump it while iterating before delivery.

minVersion.description: Minimum dsh-ee version that can install this extension. Usually omitted; set it only when you actually rely on a feature available in a specific version.

name.description: Name shown to administrators and employees.

description.description: One sentence describing what this extension does.

icon.description: Icon file, as a relative path inside the extension directory.

repo.description: Source repository URL. Omit if there is none.

kind.description: Extension kind. declarative: only a manifest and an API document; dsh-ee sends the requests itself, with no code to write and nothing to deploy; service: a service deployed by the enterprise that dsh-ee calls according to the protocol; local: an npm package that runs on employees' computers. How to choose: docs/plugins.md §4.4.

openapi.description: declarative only: file name of the OpenAPI 3.x API document, as a relative path inside the extension directory. JSON and YAML are both fine; use whatever format the other side provides. Tool names come from each operation's operationId.

servers.description: declarative only: server addresses that requests may be sent to. dsh-ee only sends requests to these addresses and only sends credentials to them. The first entry is the default API base URL.

capabilities.description: Which agreed endpoints the service extension implements. Extensions written with the SDK generate this automatically. Declarative extensions only have tools, so it can be omitted.

kb.description: Search and read the knowledge base as the current employee

notify.description: Send notifications or to-dos to employees

permissions.description: Things the extension may do when calling back into dsh-ee; each item is shown to the administrator during installation. Declarative extensions have no code, so do not write this. Request only what you need.

config.description: Configuration filled in by the administrator during installation.

type.description: kb: select a knowledge base; app: select an app; secret: secret value, stored encrypted and never echoed back.

default.description: Default value. The secret type cannot have a default.

options.description: Options for select: an array, or 'dynamic' (provided by the service extension's options endpoint; declarative extensions cannot use it).

credential.description: Whose identity to use for calls (docs/plugins.md §7, docs/ee-jwt.md). Omit for no credentials.

mode.description: shared: a single shared credential configured by the administrator, suitable for read-only public data; user_secret: each employee provides their own token; ee_jwt: dsh-ee signs a 5-minute JWT for the current employee and the other side verifies it with JWKS; oauth: the employee authorizes once, then dsh-ee stores the token per person and refreshes it before expiry (configure oauth, or have the service extension implement the oauth agreed endpoint). Prefer ee_jwt when the other side can verify JWTs.

header.description: Which request header carries the credential: in ee_jwt / user_secret mode it is the employee identity; in shared mode it is the shared credential. If a name is set, the value is placed verbatim in that header without a Bearer prefix. If omitted: employee identity uses Authorization: Bearer <value>; shared mode is chosen by the administrator during installation (default Authorization: Bearer).

audience.description: ee_jwt only: the token aud, checked by the other side when verifying the signature. Defaults to the connection name.

claims.description: ee_jwt only: which employee claims to include in addition to id, username, name, and email. Omit if not needed.

hint.description: user_secret only: tells employees where to obtain this credential.

shared.description: Set this when a shared credential (for example a service account API key) must also be sent in addition to the employee identity. Only the header it goes in is declared here; the credential value is filled in by the administrator during installation, so do not add another config item for it. The two credentials must not go in the same request header.

header.description: Request header name when type is header.

tools.description: Tools. In declarative extensions, each item supplements one endpoint in the API document; endpoints not listed follow the API document defaults (only GET is considered read-only).

name.description: In declarative extensions, this is the endpoint operationId.

description.description: Description shown to the model. When the API document description is poor, rewrite it here: what it queries, when to use it, and what it returns.

readOnly.description: Set to true only for read-only tools. Anything not marked is treated as a write operation and requires employee confirmation before the call. Do not mark endpoints that modify data as read-only.

name.description: Declarative extensions: name of a path or query parameter of the endpoint; a field in the JSON request body is written as body.<field> (first level only). List only the parameters you want to supplement or constrain; unlisted ones follow the API document.

type.description: Defaults to the type in the API document.

description.description: Description shown to the model, overriding the one in the API document.

label.description: Required when fill is app or admin: the name shown to whoever fills it in.

fill.description: Who fills in this parameter. model (default): the model fills it in. app: fixed in the app configuration by the person building the app; the model cannot see or change it, and different apps may use different values. admin: set once by the administrator when installing the extension and applied to everyone and every app; the model also cannot see it. It appears directly in the install-time configuration form (named by label), so there is no need to write it again in config, and when the same parameter appears on several tools it is filled in only once. Use admin for values that are the same across the whole enterprise (company code, tenant); use app for values that may differ per app (project, scope). app and admin parameters do not appear in the tool definitions given to the model, and required in the API document does not need to be changed.

default.description: Pre-filled value when fill is app or admin. The person filling it in (administrator, app builder) can change it; the model and employees cannot. The JSON type must match the parameter type: quote strings, but do not quote numbers or true / false. The default for the same admin parameter must be identical across tools. Do not set it for parameters the model fills in.

keep.description: Keep only these fields in the result to control the size returned to the model. Write first-level field names: if the result is an object, keep those fields; if it is an array, keep those fields of each item. When the list is wrapped one level ({"items": [...], "total": 1}), write 'field.subfield' down to the second level: items.id, items.title, and also include the first-level total you want to keep. If you do not know which fields the result contains (the API document has no responses), do not write this.

fields.description: Extension fields this extension adds (docs/access-control.md §6.0). They are created after administrator confirmation during installation; field names are prefixed with the extension, so they never collide with other fields.

object.description: Which kind of object the field is added to

options.description: Options for select / tags; levels from low to high for level

access.description: Used for access control: only select / tags / level

protocol.description: Protocol version implemented by the service extension (docs/extension-protocol.md); filled in automatically when using the SDK. Defaults to 1 when omitted.

oauth.description: When the credential mode is oauth: parameters of the standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow; dsh-ee performs the redirects, token exchange, and refresh itself; client_id / client_secret are filled in by the administrator during installation. For systems with a non-standard flow, use a service extension that implements the oauth agreed endpoint instead of this item.

apps.description: Bundled app files, as relative paths inside the extension directory. The administrator chooses whether to import them during installation.

checkIgnore.description: Check items that have been confirmed to be fine and should no longer be reported. Only check items marked 'can be ignored' qualify, and a reason must be given.

tool.description: Ignore only on this tool (by tool name). Recommended: reordering tools does not affect it.

where.description: Ignore only at this location: must match where in the check result; you may write only the part after #. If neither tool nor where is set, the whole check item is ignored.

reason.description: Why it can be ignored. Shown verbatim to the administrator installing the extension.
